nodes.body: The new index does not preserve tolerance-aware point matching. `GamaPoint.equals` uses the configured tolerance, while its hash uses exact coordinates (GamaPoint.java:427–432, 656–660). A query point equal to a stored vertex can therefore resolve to -1 and make `shortestPathRecur` index `backtrace` out of bounds. Also, when two tolerance-equal points occupy different hash buckets, `putIfAbsent` retains separate indices instead of the first equal index, changing edge initialization and routes even on successful lookups. Preserve first-equal resolution in both `lazyCalculateMatrix` and `getShortestPathImpl`, for example by retaining `vertices.indexOf` for point endpoints; falling back only on hash misses is insufficient.
Preserved first-equal, tolerance-aware lookup for point vertices in matrix initialization and shortest-path endpoint resolution. Committed as `933a7efcb`.

The hash lookup changes matching for point vertices. `GamaPoint.equals` uses the configured point tolerance, but `hashCode` uses exact coordinates (GamaPoint.java:427–432, 656–660). With tolerance 0.001, a target `{1.0005,0}` can match stored `{1,0}` through `indexOf` but return -1 here. From source index 0, the out-of-bounds matrix read then returns 0 and this method returns an empty route. A hash hit can also select a later tolerance-equal vertex instead of the first one. Preserve first-equal lookup; restoring `indexOf` fixes both cases, whereas a fallback only on hash misses does not.

The previous membership check was already hash-based: `GamaGraph.getEdges()` wraps `edgeMap.keySet()` (GamaGraph.java:871–872, 1201), and `GamaListCollectionWrapper` delegates collection operations to that set. Copying every edge into another `HashSet` adds O(E) work and storage on each query reaching this branch without improving membership complexity, even when no candidate passes the filter. Reuse the existing edge set instead.

Every search reaching this block allocates two full-grid arrays, even when the first neighboring cell contains the answer. A million-cell grid therefore allocates two million boolean entries per call instead of bookkeeping proportional to the cells explored. These buffers are reused between rings, not between queries, so repeated local `closest_to` queries can create substantial allocation and garbage-collection pressure. Maintain sparse visited/current-ring sets incrementally, or use a concurrency-safe reusable workspace, rather than allocating full-grid buffers for every local search.
Replaced the per-query full-grid buffers with sparse visited/current-ring sets in aa180523f.

When successive requests increase a cell's radius one ring at a time, geometric growth can allocate beyond `required`, but the `finally` block immediately copies the buffer again to trim it. The next request starts from that exact-sized array and repeats the process, adding a second full-buffer copy compared with the previous implementation. Allocate exactly `required` on the final ring, while retaining geometric growth for intermediate rings, to avoid this regression without exposing unused array entries.
